new_method.method:
Open Problems: On-device or low-VRAM fine-tuning of sub-billion-parameter language models (e.g. 100 M–700 M) is still impractical on 4-8 GB GPUs/NPUs.  Existing methods each tackle a single memory component – activation replay (reversible nets, checkpointing), activation storage (VeLoRA, rank-k projection), gradient storage (Few-Bit Backward, MS-BP), or optimizer state (8-bit, Any-Precision).  When naively combined they collide (e.g. reversible blocks need full-precision checkpoints; activation projection breaks LayerNorm statistics) and no planner decides which compression to apply per layer under a strict memory budget.  A unified, budget-aware training recipe that co-optimises all memory sources while preserving accuracy for small LMs is missing.
Methods: We propose Unified Compressed Training (UCT).  Core ideas:
1. Layer-wise Hybrid Compression Library (HCL)
   • Every Transformer block exposes three pluggable variants:  (A) reversible computation (no activations, extra compute),  (B) VeLoRA-style rank-1 sub-token projection (1-D stored activations),  (C) normal store.  
   • Point-wise activations inside each variant use Few-Bit Backward (3-bit derivative tables).
   • Optimizer states are kept in Any-Precision 8→4→2-bit format with incremental up-scaling if training diverges.
2. Budget-Aware Planner (BAP)
   • Static analysis of the computation graph (cheap PyTorch trace) estimates per-layer memory/compute for each variant with analytical formulas (no ILP).  
   • A greedy knapsack algorithm selects the cheapest set of variants that fits a user-specified VRAM budget B, prioritising bottom layers for projection (sensitive to semantics) and top layers for reversibility (larger activations).
   • Planner outputs a per-layer policy ⟨variant, bit-width⟩ written into the model before training starts.
3. Runtime Engine
   • Custom Autograd Functions implement reversible + projected activations together, so a layer can switch between them with one flag.
   • A tiny controller monitors actual peak memory; if it exceeds B the controller live-switches the worst-case layer from projection to reversible, guaranteeing no OOM.
4. API:  model = uct.wrap(model, budget=4*GB, rank=1, bits=3)  – drop-in for HuggingFace models.
Experimental Setup: Models:  (i) MobileLLM-350 M,  (ii) LLaMA-0.5 B distilled,  (iii) T5-small-110 M.
Datasets / Tasks:  GLUE (all tasks), Alpaca-52 K instruction fine-tune, WikiText-2 language modelling.
Hardware:  single RTX-2060-6 GB and Jetson Orin 8 GB.
Baselines:  Full FT, LoRA-8 r, MEFT (rev-adapter), VeLoRA( rank-1 ), Few-Bit Backward(3-bit), MONET schedule, and naive combo VeLoRA+LoRA.
Metrics:
• Peak resident GPU memory (PyTorch profiler)
• Tokens/s and wall-clock epoch time
• Task accuracy / Perplexity drop vs Full FT
• Additional compute overhead (%)
Ablations:  (1) remove BAP planner (uniform policy),  (2) disable optimizer quantisation,  (3) vary derivative bit-width 2–4,  (4) planner adaptive vs static.
Robustness:  repeat each run with 3 seeds; measure convergence curves and sensitivity to learning-rate sweeps.
Result: Expected:  
• UCT fits MobileLLM-350 M fine-tuning inside 4 GB VRAM (baseline LoRA needs 7 GB) with <0.4 % GLUE average drop and 15 % extra compute.  
• On LLaMA-0.5 B UCT cuts peak memory by 68 % over best single method (VeLoRA) and 44 % over MONET while matching perplexity within 0.3.  
• Planner ablation shows +1.2 GB memory and 0.6 % accuracy loss, proving necessity of layer-wise policy.  
• Runtime controller prevents OOM in 100 % of stress-tests with ≤2 % throughput penalty.  
• Derivative 3-bit vs full-precision shows negligible (<0.1) GLUE score change.
Conclusion: UCT delivers the first end-to-end, budget-aware training toolkit that jointly compresses activations, gradients and optimizer state, enabling practical on-device fine-tuning of sub-billion LMs on 4-8 GB hardware.  Academically, it demonstrates that heterogeneous layer policies outperform uniform compression and that combining reversible execution with activation projection is feasible.  Practically, UCT can be integrated into mobile inference libraries (e.g., ExecuTorch) to support user-customised fine-tuning without cloud resources.  Future work: extend planner to handle mixed-precision weight quantisation and to learn policies via reinforcement learning, and apply UCT to vision-language or speech Transformers for fully on-device personalisation.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Below are three complementary, Python-feasible experiments that jointly validate UCT from memory, accuracy, planner quality, and runtime robustness perspectives. Each plan includes goals, setup, procedures, metrics, success criteria, and minimal harness code you can adapt.

============================================================
Experiment 1 — Budget-sweep vs baselines (memory–accuracy–throughput trade-off)
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Validate that UCT achieves sub-4–6 GB fine-tuning on sub-billion LMs with minimal accuracy/perplexity loss and controllable compute overhead, outperforming single-method baselines.

Models & Datasets
- Models: MobileLLM-350M; LLaMA-0.5B (distilled); T5-small-110M
- Datasets/Tasks:
  - GLUE (MNLI, QQP, SST-2 for fast cycle; run full GLUE for final numbers)
  - Alpaca-52k (instruction finetuning; use 5–10k subset for quick iteration, full 52k for final)
  - WikiText-2 (LM perplexity)

Hardware
- Primary: RTX 2060 6 GB
- Replication: Jetson Orin 8 GB (optional: confirm portability)

Baselines
- Full FT (if fits), LoRA-8r, MEFT (rev-adapter), VeLoRA (rank-1), Few-Bit Backward (3-bit), MONET schedule, naive combo VeLoRA+LoRA.

Independent Variables
- Budget B ∈ {3 GB, 4 GB, 5 GB, 6 GB} on RTX 2060 (and 6–8 GB on Orin)
- Sequence length: 512 for GLUE; 1024 for WikiText-2; 1024 for Alpaca
- Micro-batch size: maximize without OOM (fixed across methods per budget)
- UCT: rank=1, bits=3, Any-Precision optimizer on; BAP enabled

Dependent Variables (Metrics)
- Peak resident GPU memory (torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved/allocated)
- Throughput (tokens/s), wall-clock epoch time
- Task metrics: GLUE avg (acc/F1 per task), Alpaca: instruction eval set accuracy/bleu/rouge or simple task success rate; WikiText-2: test perplexity
- Additional compute overhead (%) vs LoRA (time per token)

Procedure
1) For each budget B and model/dataset combination, configure UCT via uct.wrap(model, budget=B, rank=1, bits=3). Fix seed= {0,1,2}.
2) Choose the largest micro-batch that fits for baseline LoRA; hold constant across methods under the same B.
3) Train for N steps or to convergence budget (e.g., GLUE 3 epochs, WikiText-2 50k steps or early-stop by val ppl).
4) Log peak GPU memory, throughput, training time, and evaluation metrics per epoch.
5) Repeat for all baselines with their recommended settings; ensure fair AMP/mixed precision usage across methods.

Success Criteria
- UCT fits MobileLLM-350M at B=4 GB with <0.4% GLUE drop versus Full FT and ≤15% extra compute.
- On LLaMA-0.5B WikiText-2, UCT reduces peak memory ≥60% vs best single method (e.g., VeLoRA) with perplexity within 0.3.
- Across budgets, UCT Pareto-dominates or matches baselines on memory-accuracy trade-off.

Minimal Python Harness (sketch)

import os, time, math, json, random
import torch
import numpy as np
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
# from uct import wrap as uct_wrap  # assumed available

SEEDS = [0,1,2]

def set_seed(seed):
    random.seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed); torch.manual_seed(seed); torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

def peak_mem_gb():
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return max(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved())/2**30

def prepare_glue(task="mnli"):
    ds = load_dataset("glue", task)
    return ds

def eval_wikitext2_ppl(model, tokenizer, ds):
    model.eval()
    nll, tok = 0.0, 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for ex in ds["test"]:
            ids = tokenizer(ex["text"], return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=1024).input_ids.cuda()
            out = model(ids, labels=ids)
            nll += float(out.loss) * ids.numel()
            tok += ids.numel()
    return math.exp(nll / max(tok,1))

def train_one(model, tokenizer, train_ds, eval_fn, method_name, outdir, max_steps=2000):
    args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=outdir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=os.environ.get("BATCH", 1),
        gradient_accumulation_steps=int(os.environ.get("GAS", 1)),
        eval_strategy="steps", eval_steps=200, logging_steps=50, save_steps=0,
        learning_rate=2e-5, num_train_epochs=1, fp16=True,
        report_to=[]
    )
    trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=train_ds)
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    t0 = time.time(); trainer.train(); t1 = time.time()
    mem_gb = peak_mem_gb(); dt = t1 - t0
    return {"method": method_name, "mem_gb": mem_gb, "time_s": dt}

# Example loop (pseudo):
# for B in [3,4,5,6]:
#   model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("<llama-0.5b>").cuda()
#   tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("<llama-0.5b>")
#   model = uct_wrap(model, budget=B*2**30, rank=1, bits=3)  # UCT
#   res = train_one(model, tokenizer, train_ds, eval_fn, method_name=f"UCT_B{B}", outdir=f"./runs/UCT_B{B}")
#   print(res)

Notes
- Use AMP for all methods. Ensure LoRA/MONET configs follow their papers.
- Control for optimizer, LR, schedulers where possible; report any deviations.
- Record tokens/s: total_tokens/epoch_time.

============================================================
Experiment 2 — Planner (BAP) ablation and layer-policy quality
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Show the necessity and correctness of BAP: layer-wise hybrid policies beat uniform compression; BAP’s memory estimates match actuals; disabling optimizer quantization or using different derivative bit-widths impacts memory more than accuracy.

Conditions
- Model: MobileLLM-350M on GLUE (MNLI, SST-2) and LLaMA-0.5B on WikiText-2
- Budget: tight regime where naive methods struggle (e.g., 4 GB)

Variants
- UCT+BAP (full system)
- UCT w/o BAP: uniform policy (same variant for all layers), with 3 sub-variants:
  - Uniform reversible (A-only)
  - Uniform projection (B-only)
  - Uniform normal store (C-only) if it fits
- UCT+BAP but optimizer quantization off (full-precision states)
- UCT+BAP with derivative bits ∈ {2,3,4}
- UCT+BAP static vs adaptive (planner-only vs planner+runtime updates)

Measurements
- Peak memory, throughput, task metric (GLUE avg / ppl), additional compute overhead
- Policy quality: per-layer variant map; fraction of bottom layers projected and top layers reversible
- Planner accuracy: relative error between planned peak memory and measured peak (MAPE)

Procedure
1) Enable logging of per-layer policy from BAP before training (variant, bit-width per layer) and write to JSON.
2) Train each variant with 3 seeds; record metrics and policies.
3) Plot/print memory vs accuracy for each variant; show BAP’s policy follows the expected bottom→projection, top→reversible trend.
4) Compute and report MAPE between BAP-forecasted peak memory and actual measured peak.

Success Criteria
- Removing BAP increases peak memory by ≥1 GB and causes ≥0.5% GLUE avg drop (or similar) under the same budget.
- BAP’s planned peak memory within 10–15% of actual.
- Derivative 3-bit vs FP shows ≤0.1 GLUE change; 2-bit stays stable with minor loss; 4-bit negligible change and higher memory.
- Optimizer quantization off: peak memory increases significantly with ≤0.1–0.2 drop in accuracy relative to quantized.

Minimal Hooks (sketch)

# Assuming uct exposes planner APIs
# from uct.planner import get_planned_policy, set_uniform_policy

def run_with_policy(model, budget, policy_mode, der_bits=3, opt_quant=True):
    # policy_mode: "bap", "uniform_rev", "uniform_proj", "uniform_store"
    if policy_mode == "bap":
        m = uct_wrap(model, budget=budget, rank=1, bits=der_bits, opt_quant=opt_quant, planner="greedy")
        policy = uct.get_policy(m)
    else:
        m = uct_wrap(model, budget=budget, rank=1, bits=der_bits, opt_quant=opt_quant, planner=None)
        if policy_mode == "uniform_rev":
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="reversible")
        elif policy_mode == "uniform_proj":
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="projection")
        else:
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="store")
        policy = uct.get_policy(m)
    with open("policy.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(policy, f, indent=2)
    # proceed to train_one(...), record memory and accuracy

# Planner accuracy
# planned_peak = uct.estimate_peak_memory(model)
# actual_peak = peak_mem_gb()
# mape = abs(planned_peak - actual_peak)/actual_peak

============================================================
Experiment 3 — Runtime controller OOM-prevention stress test
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Demonstrate that UCT’s runtime controller prevents OOM under dynamic workloads (varying sequence lengths and micro-batch sizes) with ≤2% throughput penalty.

Setup
- Model: LLaMA-0.5B (distilled) on Alpaca-52k or WikiText-2
- Start with budget near device limit (e.g., B=5.5 GB on a 6 GB GPU)
- Enable runtime controller.

Stressors
- Curriculum that increases sequence length: 512→1024→1536→2048 over training phases
- Aggressive micro-batch selection normalized per phase; keep other hyperparams fixed
- Alternate spiky batches: interleave long-context samples to create peak-usage variance

Variants
- UCT with controller ON (default)
- UCT with controller OFF (same BAP plan, no live switches)
- Baseline VeLoRA (or LoRA) at same micro-batch and curriculum, for reference

Measurements
- Count of runs that hit OOM (OutOfMemoryError) across 3 seeds
- Throughput (tokens/s) before/after live-switch events; total penalty percentage
- Task metric trajectory (loss/ppl) to confirm no degradation from live switching
- Log which layers switched and how often

Procedure
1) Implement a training loop that catches OOM, logs it, and resumes if possible; for UCT-ON record controller events (layer switches, time, and memory readings).
2) Sweep max_length phases every N steps; maintain target micro-batch and GAS.
3) Repeat each variant with 3 seeds; aggregate OOM occurrence rate and throughput penalty.

Success Criteria
- UCT-ON prevents OOM in ~100% of runs; OFF and baselines experience OOMs at long contexts.
- Throughput penalty ≤2% averaged over the run; accuracy/perplexity unaffected compared to OFF on phases where OFF survives.

Minimal Stress Harness (sketch)

def stress_train(model, tokenizer, dataset, controller_on=True):
    model = uct_wrap(model, budget=int(5.5*2**30), rank=1, bits=3, planner="greedy", controller=controller_on)
    max_lens = [512, 1024, 1536, 2048]
    oom_count = 0
    tokens = 0
    t0 = time.time()
    for L in max_lens:
        try:
            for step in range(500):
                batch = sample_batch(dataset, tokenizer, max_length=L)
                torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
                out = model(**batch)
                out.loss.backward()
                optimizer.step(); optimizer.zero_grad()
                tokens += int(batch["input_ids"].numel())
        except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
            oom_count += 1
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            if not controller_on:
                break
    t1 = time.time()
    thpt = tokens / (t1 - t0)
    return {"ooms": oom_count, "thpt": thpt, "peak_gb": peak_mem_gb()}

# Compare controller_on=True vs False and a baseline method.

============================================================
Analysis & Reporting (common to all experiments)
============================================================
- Repeat each configuration with 3 seeds; report mean ± std.
- Provide convergence curves (loss/ppl over steps) to verify stability and optimizer-quantization up-scaling events (if any).
- Summarize:
  - Memory vs accuracy/perplexity Pareto fronts across budgets (Exp 1)
  - Policy maps and planner accuracy, plus ablation outcomes (Exp 2)
  - OOM counts and throughput penalty under stress (Exp 3)

Potential Pitfalls and Mitigations
- Mixed-precision inconsistencies across baselines: enforce autocast and GradScaler uniformly.
- Dataloader bottlenecks: pre-tokenize datasets, pin_memory=True.
- Fair micro-batch selection: choose max that fits for baseline and reuse across methods per budget.
- Jetson differences: may require smaller batches and avoiding unsupported kernels; measure "torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved" on Orin.

Expected Outcomes (aligned with the paper’s claims)
- UCT fits MobileLLM-350M at 4 GB with <0.4% GLUE drop and ~15% compute overhead vs LoRA.
- On LLaMA-0.5B WikiText-2, UCT cuts peak memory by ~68% vs VeLoRA and ~44% vs MONET with ≤0.3 ppl delta.
- Planner ablation increases peak memory by ~1.2 GB and degrades GLUE by ~0.6%.
- Runtime controller eliminates OOMs in all stress runs with ≤2% throughput penalty.
experimental_design.experiment_details:
Below is a complete, implementation-oriented experimental plan that follows the three experiments in the Experiment Strategy, fills in missing practical details, and supplies runnable PyTorch/Transformers code sketches. I assume a “uct” Python package exposing uct.wrap and simple planner/runtime APIs as described in New Methods. Where third-party baselines are not available as pip packages, I give near-equivalent configurations using widely available libraries (Transformers, PEFT, bitsandbytes, fairscale/xFormers for reversible/checkpointing), and call out optional or best-effort implementations.

============================================================
Common setup (applies to all experiments)
============================================================
- Environment
  - Python ≥3.10, PyTorch ≥2.2, CUDA 11.8+, transformers ≥4.41, datasets ≥2.19, evaluate, peft ≥0.11, bitsandbytes ≥0.43, accelerate, scikit-learn, wandb (optional), fairscale (for reversible sequence, optional), xformers (optional for speed), uct (our method, assumed available).
  - Install: pip install -U torch torchvision torchaudio transformers datasets evaluate peft bitsandbytes accelerate scikit-learn wandb fairscale xformers

- Hardware
  - Primary: NVIDIA RTX 2060 (6 GB). Optional replication: Jetson Orin 8 GB (ensure torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved is available; avoid kernels not supported on Orin; use torch.compile(False)).

- Models (public substitutes if named ones are unavailable)
  - MobileLLM-350M proxy: gpt2-medium (~355M) or EleutherAI/pythia-410m (410M) for causal LM; for GLUE classification a small encoder like roberta-base can be used only if you want encoder baselines; however to keep architecture consistent, prefer causal LMs for LM tasks and T5 for GLUE.
  - LLaMA-0.5B (distilled) proxy: EleutherAI/pythia-510m (≈500M).
  - T5-small-110M: t5-small (for GLUE, seq2seq framing).

- Datasets
  - GLUE: hf datasets "glue" with tasks {mnli, sst2, qqp}. For full GLUE, run all tasks after initial cycles.
  - WikiText-2: "wikitext", name="wikitext-2-raw-v1".
  - Alpaca-52k: tatsu-lab/alpaca (SFT; use 5–10k subset for iteration).

- Tokenization and data collators
  - GLUE: use DataCollatorWithPadding for classification, pad-to-multiple-of=8 for Tensor Cores.
  - LM tasks (WikiText-2/Alpaca): use DataCollatorForLanguageModeling with mlm=False for Causal LM; for T5, use Seq2Seq collator and task-specific templates.

- Mixed precision and fairness controls
  - Use torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler for custom loops; or HF Trainer with fp16=True or bf16=True if supported. Keep identical precision across methods.
  - Optimizer: AdamW (transformers default) for Full FT/LoRA; bitsandbytes Adam8bit for 8-bit optimizer baseline; UCT uses its Any-Precision optimizer inside uct.wrap (assumed). Keep LR, scheduler, weight decay, and warmup consistent.
  - Gradient clipping: clip_norm=1.0 for all methods.

- Reproducibility
  - Seeds: {0,1,2}. Set torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True, cudnn.benchmark=False (may reduce throughput slightly but increases reproducibility).

- Memory and throughput measurement
  - Before each train run: torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(); measure peak with max(max_memory_allocated, max_memory_reserved) / 2**30.
  - Tokens/s = sum(batch_input_ids.numel()) / wall_clock_time_seconds, counted only during training steps.

- Micro-batch selection under budgets
  - For a given budget B and method, run a small binary search to find the largest per-device micro-batch size that fits without OOM at the target max_length. Fix micro-batch per method per B; for fairness, hold micro-batch constant across methods for the same B if possible; if a method cannot fit the chosen micro-batch at B, reduce for all methods to the next feasible level or report capacity differences explicitly.

- Logging
  - Write a JSON per run with: model, dataset, budget, seed, micro-batch, GAS, precision, optimizer, method, peak_mem_gb, tokens_per_s, epoch_time_s, eval metrics (per task), and wall clock.
  - Optional: log to wandb for live monitoring.

- Baselines implementable with common libraries
  - Full fine-tuning (Full FT): standard training with all weights trainable, AMP on, AdamW.
  - LoRA (PEFT): peft.LoraConfig with r=8, lora_alpha=16, lora_dropout=0.05; target modules customized per model (e.g., attn qkv and out proj, MLP gate/up/down).
  - 8-bit optimizer: bitsandbytes.optim.Adam8bit.
  - Gradient checkpointing: model.gradient_checkpointing_enable() or torch.utils.checkpoint on blocks.
  - Reversible layers (optional baseline support): fairscale.nn.reversible.ReversibleSequence for compatible architectures (easiest for custom Transformer stacks; not trivial for HF pretrained heads; include only if feasible).
  - MONET schedule and VeLoRA (rank-1 activation projection), Few-Bit Backward: if official repos are available, integrate them; otherwise, report as “not run” or mark as UCT components only. For fairness, you can replace MONET with a strong checkpointing + 8-bit optimizer baseline.

- UCT usage (assumed API)
  - model = uct.wrap(model, budget=B, rank=1, bits=3, planner="greedy", opt_quant=True, controller=True)
  - uct.get_policy(model) -> per-layer policy list with fields {layer_id, variant ∈ {reversible, projection, store}, bits}
  - uct.estimate_peak_memory(model) -> planned peak bytes
  - uct.set_uniform_policy(model, variant) to override


============================================================
Experiment 1 — Budget-sweep vs baselines (memory–accuracy–throughput trade-off)
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Validate that UCT achieves sub-4–6 GB fine-tuning on sub-billion LMs with minimal accuracy/ppl loss and controllable compute overhead, outperforming single-method baselines.

Models & Tasks
- Causal LM:
  - Pythia-510M on WikiText-2 (LM perplexity) and Alpaca-52k subset (SFT loss or instruction eval subset).
  - GPT2-medium (~355M) as MobileLLM-350M proxy on GLUE-sst2 (for classification via causal LM head with prompt) and WikiText-2.
- Encoder-Decoder:
  - T5-small-110M on GLUE (mnli, sst2, qqp). For T5, use Seq2SeqTrainer and appropriate tokenization (text-to-text framing for GLUE, or HuggingFace GLUE-T5 templates).

Budgets and sequences
- RTX 2060 (6 GB): B ∈ {3 GB, 4 GB, 5 GB, 6 GB}.
- Sequence lengths: 512 for GLUE, 1024 for WikiText-2 and Alpaca (final long-context tests can be 1536–2048 but keep 1024 here).

Training hyperparameters (default; tune per model lightly if needed)
- Optimizer: AdamW, lr=2e-5 (GLUE), lr=1e-4 (LM), betas=(0.9,0.98), weight_decay=0.01.
- Scheduler: linear decay with 5% warmup.
- Epochs: GLUE 3 epochs; WikiText-2 50k steps or 3 epochs over pre-tokenized shards; Alpaca 3 epochs over 10k subset (final run full 52k).
- AMP: fp16 on RTX; bf16 if supported on Orin.
- Grad clip: 1.0.
- Early stopping: optional patience=3 based on validation.

Baselines
- Full FT (if it fits under B) + AMP.
- LoRA r=8 via PEFT + AMP.
- 8-bit optimizer: bitsandbytes Adam8bit.
- Checkpointing baseline: model.gradient_checkpointing_enable() + AdamW.
- Optional: QLoRA (bnb 4-bit weights + LoRA) as an extra strong low-memory baseline on LM tasks only.
- MONET, VeLoRA, Few-Bit Backward: run if repo available; otherwise note.

UCT settings
- uct.wrap(..., budget=B, rank=1, bits=3, planner="greedy", opt_quant=True, controller=True)
- GAS and micro-batch: determined by binary search per B; keep constant across methods under same B if feasible.

Metrics
- Peak GPU memory (GB).
- Throughput (tokens/s) and wall-clock epoch time.
- GLUE: accuracy/F1 per task; report average.
- WikiText-2: test perplexity.
- Alpaca: simple held-out instruction set exact-match or RougeL (optional), or average loss on eval split.
- Additional compute overhead (%) vs LoRA time/token.

Procedure
1) For each budget B and model/task, pick largest micro-batch that fits with LoRA at target sequence length; fix for all methods if possible.
2) Train each method with 3 seeds; record metrics and averages.
3) For T5 GLUE, ensure consistent data templates and label mapping.
4) For LM tasks, pre-tokenize dataset offline to reduce loader overhead (map batched tokenizer, save to disk cache).

Success criteria (as in New Methods)
- UCT fits “350M” proxy at 4 GB with <0.4% GLUE avg drop vs Full FT and ≤15% extra compute.
- On ~0.5B LM, UCT reduces peak memory ≥60% vs VeLoRA (if available) or strong single baseline, with ppl within 0.3.
- Across B, UCT Pareto-dominates or matches baselines on memory-accuracy.

Minimal Python harness (Trainer-based; extensible)

import os, time, json, math, random
import numpy as np
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoTokenizer,
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    AutoModelForSequenceClassification,
    AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM,
    DataCollatorForLanguageModeling,
    DataCollatorWithPadding,
    Trainer, TrainingArguments,
)
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
# from uct import wrap as uct_wrap, get_policy, estimate_peak_memory  # assumed available

SEEDS = [0,1,2]

def set_seed(seed):
    random.seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed); torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False

def peak_mem_gb():
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return max(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved())/2**30

# ---------- Data prep ----------

def get_wikitext2(tokenizer, block_size=1024):
    ds = load_dataset("wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1")
    def tok_fn(ex):
        return tokenizer(ex["text"])  # defer chunking
    tok = ds.map(tok_fn, batched=True, remove_columns=ds["train"].column_names)
    # group texts into block_size
    def group_texts(examples):
        concatenated = {}
        for k in examples.keys():
            concatenated[k] = sum(examples[k], [])
        total_length = (len(concatenated["input_ids"]) // block_size) * block_size
        result = {
            k: [t[i:i+block_size] for i in range(0, total_length, block_size)]
            for k, t in concatenated.items()
        }
        result["labels"] = result["input_ids"].copy()
        return result
    chunked = tok.map(group_texts, batched=True)
    return chunked

def get_alpaca_subset(tokenizer, n=10000, max_length=1024):
    ds = load_dataset("tatsu-lab/alpaca")
    ds = ds["train"].select(range(min(n, len(ds["train"]))))
    def format_and_tok(ex):
        prompt = f"Instruction: {ex['instruction']}\nInput: {ex.get('input','')}\nResponse:"
        target = ex["output"]
        text = prompt + target
        ids = tokenizer(text, truncation=True, max_length=max_length)
        # simple causal labels = input_ids
        ids["labels"] = ids["input_ids"].copy()
        return ids
    tok = ds.map(format_and_tok, remove_columns=ds.column_names)
    return tok.train_test_split(test_size=0.02)

def get_glue(task, tokenizer, max_length=512, model_type="seqcls"):
    ds = load_dataset("glue", task)
    # task-specific fields
    task_to_keys = {
        "sst2": ("sentence", None),
        "mnli": ("premise", "hypothesis"),
        "qqp": ("question1", "question2"),
    }
    sentence1_key, sentence2_key = task_to_keys[task]
    def tok_fn(ex):
        args = (ex[sentence1_key],) if sentence2_key is None else (ex[sentence1_key], ex[sentence2_key])
        return tokenizer(*args, truncation=True, max_length=max_length)
    tok = ds.map(tok_fn, batched=True)
    if model_type == "t5":
        # T5 expects text-to-text; skipping full templating for brevity
        pass
    return tok

# ---------- Models ----------

def load_causal(model_name):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, use_fast=True)
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    mdl = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
    mdl.resize_token_embeddings(len(tok))
    return mdl, tok

def load_seqcls(model_name, num_labels):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, use_fast=True)
    mdl = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name, num_labels=num_labels, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
    return mdl, tok

# ---------- LoRA baseline helper ----------

def apply_lora(model, model_type="gpt2"):
    if model_type in ["gpt2", "pythia"]:
        target_modules = ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "fc_in", "fc_out", "up_proj", "down_proj"]
    else:
        target_modules = ["q", "v", "k", "o", "wi", "wo"]
    cfg = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, lora_dropout=0.05, bias="none", target_modules=target_modules, task_type=None)
    lora_model = get_peft_model(model, cfg)
    return lora_model

# ---------- Training ----------

def train_with_trainer(model, train_ds, eval_ds, tokenizer, outdir, per_device_bs=1, gas=1, lr=2e-5, steps=None, epochs=3, fp16=True):
    args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=outdir,
        per_device_train_batch_size=per_device_bs,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=per_device_bs,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=gas,
        evaluation_strategy="epoch" if eval_ds is not None else "no",
        logging_steps=50,
        save_strategy="no",
        learning_rate=lr,
        num_train_epochs=epochs if steps is None else 1,
        max_steps=steps if steps is not None else -1,
        warmup_ratio=0.05,
        fp16=fp16,
        bf16=False,
        report_to=[],
        dataloader_pin_memory=True,
    )
    trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=train_ds, eval_dataset=eval_ds, tokenizer=tokenizer)
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    t0 = time.time(); trainer.train(); t1 = time.time()
    mem_gb = peak_mem_gb(); dt = t1 - t0
    thpt = getattr(trainer.state, "train_samples_per_second", None)
    res = {"mem_gb": mem_gb, "time_s": dt, "samples_per_s": thpt}
    if eval_ds is not None:
        metrics = trainer.evaluate(); res.update(metrics)
    return res

# ---------- Example run loop (WikiText-2 with Pythia-510M) ----------

def run_exp1_wikitext2(budget_gb_list=(3,4,5,6)):
    model_name = "EleutherAI/pythia-510m"
    model, tok = load_causal(model_name)
    ds = get_wikitext2(tok, block_size=1024)
    collator = DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(tokenizer=tok, mlm=False)

    results = []
    for seed in SEEDS:
        set_seed(seed)
        # baseline LoRA micro-batch search per budget (simplified: try 1 then 2)
        for B in budget_gb_list:
            bs = 1
            for try_bs in [2, 3, 4, 1]:
                ok = True
                try:
                    tmp_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
                    tmp_model = apply_lora(tmp_model, model_type="pythia")
                    args = TrainingArguments(output_dir="/tmp", per_device_train_batch_size=try_bs, fp16=True, max_steps=5, report_to=[])
                    Trainer(tmp_model, args, ds["train"].select(range(64)), data_collator=collator).train()
                    mem = peak_mem_gb()
                    if mem <= B + 0.1:  # slack
                        bs = try_bs; break
                except Exception:
                    ok = False
                finally:
                    del tmp_model; torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            # Run UCT
            mdl = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
            mdl = uct_wrap(mdl, budget=int(B*2**30), rank=1, bits=3, planner="greedy", opt_quant=True, controller=True)
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            res_uct = train_with_trainer(mdl, ds["train"], ds["validation"], tok, outdir=f"./runs/uct_{B}gb_s{seed}", per_device_bs=bs)
            res_uct.update({"method": f"UCT_{B}GB", "seed": seed, "budget_gb": B})
            results.append(res_uct)
            del mdl; torch.cuda.empty_cache()

            # Run LoRA baseline
            mdl = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
            mdl = apply_lora(mdl, model_type="pythia")
            res_lora = train_with_trainer(mdl, ds["train"], ds["validation"], tok, outdir=f"./runs/lora_{B}gb_s{seed}", per_device_bs=bs)
            res_lora.update({"method": f"LoRA_{B}GB", "seed": seed, "budget_gb": B})
            results.append(res_lora)
            del mdl; torch.cuda.empty_cache()

            # Optional baselines: checkpointing + 8-bit Adam
            mdl = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
            mdl.gradient_checkpointing_enable()
            # Swap optimizer to Adam8bit via Trainer by override (requires custom Trainer or Accelerate); omitted for brevity
            res_ckpt = train_with_trainer(mdl, ds["train"], ds["validation"], tok, outdir=f"./runs/ckpt_{B}gb_s{seed}", per_device_bs=bs)
            res_ckpt.update({"method": f"CKPT_{B}GB", "seed": seed, "budget_gb": B})
            results.append(res_ckpt)
            del mdl; torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    with open("exp1_wikitext2_results.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


Notes for Experiment 1
- For GLUE with T5, use Seq2SeqTrainer and text-to-text templates; for Causal LM classification, either use an LM prompt with a verbalizer and compute accuracy on the decoded token or switch to AutoModelForSequenceClassification for encoder models. Keep architecture consistent within each comparison.
- For tokens/s, Trainer reports samples/s; you can convert to tokens/s by multiplying average sequence length per batch. Or implement a custom callback to count tokens processed.
- Additional compute overhead vs LoRA is computed as (time_per_token_UCT / time_per_token_LoRA - 1) * 100%.
- If Full FT OOMs, record as N/A at that budget.


============================================================
Experiment 2 — Planner (BAP) ablation and layer-policy quality
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Show that BAP layer-wise hybrid policies beat uniform compression and that BAP’s memory estimates match actual behavior. Also quantify sensitivity to optimizer quantization and derivative bit-widths.

Conditions
- Models: GPT2-medium (≈350M) on GLUE sst2, and Pythia-510M on WikiText-2.
- Budget: tight (4 GB), sequence length 512 (sst2) / 1024 (WikiText-2), micro-batch selected similarly as Exp 1.

Variants
- UCT+BAP (full system): planner="greedy", opt_quant=True, bits=3.
- UCT w/o BAP (uniform policies):
  - Uniform reversible (variant A-only),
  - Uniform projection (variant B-only),
  - Uniform store (variant C-only) if it fits under 4 GB.
- UCT+BAP with optimizer quantization off: opt_quant=False.
- UCT+BAP with derivative bit-widths bits ∈ {2, 3, 4}.
- UCT+BAP static vs adaptive: controller=False (static) vs controller=True (adaptive live switching) under the same initial BAP plan.

Measurements
- Peak memory, throughput, GLUE accuracy (sst2) / perplexity (WikiText-2).
- Per-layer policy map and summary: fraction of bottom layers assigned projection, top layers reversible.
- Planner accuracy: MAPE = |planned_peak - actual_peak| / actual_peak.

Procedure
1) For each model/dataset and variant, run 3 seeds.
2) Before training, extract and save policy JSON. Compute planned peak via uct.estimate_peak_memory and compare to measured peak.
3) Summarize policy quality by computing, for L layers, percentage of layers 0..L/3 using projection, and layers 2L/3..L using reversible.
4) Compare memory and task metrics across variants.

Success criteria
- Removing BAP (uniform policies) increases peak memory by ≥1 GB and causes ≥0.5% GLUE drop (or comparable degradation at fixed B).
- BAP planned peak within 10–15% of actual peak (MAPE ≤ 0.15).
- Derivative 3-bit vs FP: ≤0.1 GLUE change; 2-bit minor potential loss; 4-bit negligible change but slightly higher memory.
- Disabling optimizer quantization increases memory significantly with minor accuracy change (≤0.2).

Code hooks for policy ablations and planner accuracy

import json, time

def run_with_policy(model_name, dataset_name="sst2", budget_gb=4, policy_mode="bap", der_bits=3, opt_quant=True, controller=True):
    if dataset_name == "sst2":
        model, tok = load_seqcls(model_name, num_labels=2)
        ds = get_glue("sst2", tok, max_length=512)
        train_ds, val_ds = ds["train"], ds["validation"]
        per_device_bs = 8  # adjust after probing
        gas = 1
    else:
        model, tok = load_causal(model_name)
        ds = get_wikitext2(tok, block_size=1024)
        train_ds, val_ds = ds["train"], ds["validation"]
        per_device_bs = 1
        gas = 1

    if policy_mode == "bap":
        m = uct_wrap(model, budget=int(budget_gb*2**30), rank=1, bits=der_bits,
                     planner="greedy", opt_quant=opt_quant, controller=controller)
    else:
        m = uct_wrap(model, budget=int(budget_gb*2**30), rank=1, bits=der_bits,
                     planner=None, opt_quant=opt_quant, controller=controller)
        if policy_mode == "uniform_rev":
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="reversible")
        elif policy_mode == "uniform_proj":
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="projection")
        elif policy_mode == "uniform_store":
            uct.set_uniform_policy(m, variant="store")

    policy = uct.get_policy(m)
    with open(f"policy_{model_name}_{dataset_name}_{policy_mode}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(policy, f, indent=2)

    planned_peak = uct.estimate_peak_memory(m) / 2**30
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    res = train_with_trainer(m, train_ds, val_ds, tok, outdir=f"./runs/{policy_mode}_{dataset_name}", per_device_bs=per_device_bs, gas=gas)
    actual_peak = peak_mem_gb()
    mape = abs(planned_peak - actual_peak) / max(actual_peak, 1e-6)
    res.update({"planned_peak_gb": planned_peak, "actual_peak_gb": actual_peak, "mape": mape, "policy_mode": policy_mode})
    return res

# Example sequence of runs

def exp2():
    model_sst2 = "gpt2-medium"
    model_wt2 = "EleutherAI/pythia-510m"
    results = []
    for seed in SEEDS:
        set_seed(seed)
        for mode in ["bap", "uniform_rev", "uniform_proj", "uniform_store"]:
            try:
                res = run_with_policy(model_sst2, "sst2", 4, policy_mode=mode, der_bits=3, opt_quant=True, controller=True)
                res.update({"model": model_sst2, "task": "sst2", "seed": seed})
                results.append(res)
            except Exception as e:
                results.append({"model": model_sst2, "task": "sst2", "seed": seed, "policy_mode": mode, "error": str(e)})
        # Bits ablation
        for b in [2,3,4]:
            res = run_with_policy(model_wt2, "wikitext2", 4, policy_mode="bap", der_bits=b, opt_quant=True, controller=False)
            res.update({"model": model_wt2, "task": "wikitext2", "seed": seed, "der_bits": b})
            results.append(res)
        # Optimizer quant off
        res = run_with_policy(model_wt2, "wikitext2", 4, policy_mode="bap", der_bits=3, opt_quant=False, controller=False)
        res.update({"model": model_wt2, "task": "wikitext2", "seed": seed, "der_bits": 3, "opt_quant": False})
        results.append(res)
        # Static vs adaptive
        res = run_with_policy(model_wt2, "wikitext2", 4, policy_mode="bap", der_bits=3, opt_quant=True, controller=False)
        res.update({"model": model_wt2, "task": "wikitext2", "seed": seed, "controller": False})
        results.append(res)
        res = run_with_policy(model_wt2, "wikitext2", 4, policy_mode="bap", der_bits=3, opt_quant=True, controller=True)
        res.update({"model": model_wt2, "task": "wikitext2", "seed": seed, "controller": True})
        results.append(res)
    with open("exp2_results.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

Policy quality summary (post-processing suggestion)
- Load the saved policy JSONs and compute per-layer statistics:
  - For L transformer blocks, compute the proportion in indices [0, L/3) assigned projection, and in [2L/3, L) assigned reversible.
  - Report as percentages and visualize as a heatmap (optional).


============================================================
Experiment 3 — Runtime controller OOM-prevention stress test
============================================================
Goal / Hypothesis
- Demonstrate UCT’s runtime controller prevents OOM under dynamic workloads (varying sequence lengths and micro-batch sizes) with ≤2% throughput penalty.

Setup
- Model: Pythia-510M (proxy for 0.5B) on Alpaca-52k subset or WikiText-2.
- Budget near device limit: e.g., B = 5.5 GB on a 6 GB GPU.
- Curriculum: max_length phases 512 → 1024 → 1536 → 2048.
- Aggressive micro-batch set at the start based on 1024 feasibility; keep GAS constant.

Variants
- UCT with controller ON (default, controller=True).
- UCT with controller OFF (controller=False) using the same initial BAP plan.
- LoRA (or VeLoRA) baseline at the same micro-batch and curriculum to show OOM incidents.

Measurements
- Count OOM occurrences across phases and seeds.
- Throughput tokens/s overall and within each phase.
- Throughput penalty = (tokens/s OFF − tokens/s ON) / tokens/s OFF.
- Task metric trajectory (loss/ppl) to confirm training stability.
- Log which layers switched and how often (from uct controller event log API if available).

Procedure
- Implement a manual training loop to precisely control sequence length and catch OOM exceptions; when OOM occurs in OFF, log and abort.
- For ON, log each controller switch event (layer id, old→new variant, timestamp, memory reading).
- Repeat per seed; aggregate OOM rate and throughput penalty.

Success criteria
- Controller ON: 0 OOMs across runs; OFF and LoRA baselines OOM at longer contexts.
- Throughput penalty ≤2% average.
- No degradation in loss/ppl compared to OFF on phases where OFF survives.

Stress-test training loop (manual)

from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler

def sample_lm_batch(dataset, tokenizer, max_length, batch_size=1):
    # Simplified: sample random lines and tokenize to max_length
    import random
    items = [dataset[random.randint(0, len(dataset)-1)] for _ in range(batch_size)]
    texts = [it.get("text") or tokenizer.decode(it["input_ids"]) for it in items]
    enc = tokenizer(texts, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=max_length, padding="max_length")
    enc = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in enc.items()}
    enc["labels"] = enc["input_ids"].clone()
    return enc

def stress_train(model_name="EleutherAI/pythia-510m", controller_on=True, budget_gb=5.5, phases=(512,1024,1536,2048), steps_per_phase=300, lr=1e-4):
    model, tok = load_causal(model_name)
    # Wrap with UCT
    m = uct_wrap(model, budget=int(budget_gb*2**30), rank=1, bits=3, planner="greedy", opt_quant=True, controller=controller_on)
    scaler = GradScaler()
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(m.parameters(), lr=lr)
    ds = load_dataset("wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1")["train"]

    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    t0 = time.time()
    total_tokens = 0
    oom_count = 0
    try:
        for L in phases:
            for step in range(steps_per_phase):
                batch = sample_lm_batch(ds, tok, max_length=L, batch_size=1)
                with autocast():
                    out = m(**batch)
                    loss = out.loss
                scaler.scale(loss).backward()
                scaler.step(opt); scaler.update(); opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
                total_tokens += int(batch["input_ids"].numel())
    except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
        oom_count += 1
    t1 = time.time()
    thpt = total_tokens / (t1 - t0)
    peak = peak_mem_gb()
    # Optionally, get controller events: uct.get_controller_events(m)
    return {"controller_on": controller_on, "ooms": oom_count, "tokens_per_s": thpt, "peak_gb": peak}

# Example usage:
# res_on = stress_train(controller_on=True)
# res_off = stress_train(controller_on=False)
# json.dump([res_on, res_off], open("exp3_results.json","w"), indent=2)


============================================================
Analysis & Reporting (for all experiments)
============================================================
- Repeat each configuration with seeds {0,1,2}; report mean ± std for all metrics.
- Present tables/plots (post-processing) of:
  - Memory vs accuracy/perplexity (Pareto fronts) across budgets (Exp 1).
  - Ablation results showing memory, accuracy/ppl changes (Exp 2), along with policy heatmaps and MAPE distribution.
  - OOM incidence and throughput penalty (Exp 3), with controller switch event timelines.
- Compute additional compute overhead (%) vs LoRA by normalizing time/token.
- For UCT Any-Precision optimizer, record if/when it up-scales precision due to divergence (UCT is assumed to expose such events); correlate with learning curves.


============================================================
Reliability enhancements and fairness checks
============================================================
- Pre-tokenize and cache datasets to disk to avoid dataloader bottlenecks. Use num_workers=4, pin_memory=True.
- Normalize padding strategy across methods (pad to multiple of 8) to avoid artificial memory differences.
- Use identical LR schedules, warmup, weight decay, gradient clipping across methods.
- Ensure LoRA target_modules cover attention and MLP projections consistently for all causal LMs.
- Calibrate micro-batch under each B using the same probing procedure, then fix per method.
- Verify AMP gradient scaling is enabled for all methods; disable for none.
- On Orin, avoid unsupported fused optimizers; prefer AdamW or Adam8bit if supported; validate memory via max_memory_reserved.


============================================================
What to do if some baselines are unavailable
============================================================
- VeLoRA, MONET, Few-Bit Backward official repos: If you cannot obtain them, report primary baselines as LoRA, QLoRA (LM tasks), gradient checkpointing, and 8-bit optimizer. Where possible, include Reversible blocks via fairscale to approximate reversible memory behavior.
- Clearly label any omitted baselines and justify substitutions.


============================================================
Expected outcomes (aligned with New Methods)
============================================================
- UCT fits ~350M fine-tuning at 4 GB with <0.4% GLUE avg drop and ~15% compute overhead vs LoRA.
- On ~0.5B LM, UCT reduces peak memory by ≈68% over best single-method baseline (e.g., VeLoRA or checkpointing+8-bit) and ≈44% over MONET if available, with ppl within 0.3.
- Planner ablation increases peak memory by ≈1.2 GB and degrades GLUE by ≈0.6%; BAP planned peak within 10–15% of actual.
- Runtime controller prevents 100% OOMs under stress with ≤2% throughput penalty and stable loss trajectories.

End of specification.

# Unified Compressed Training (UCT) — Reproducible Experiments
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# This script provides end-to-end experimental code implementing:
#   - Experiment 1: Budget-sweep vs baselines (memory–accuracy–throughput)
#   - Experiment 2: Planner ablation and policy quality
#   - Experiment 3: Runtime controller OOM-prevention stress test
#
# It includes a working, minimal UCT implementation for toy Transformers
# (reversible via checkpointing, projected activations, few-bit backward,
#  and a simple Any-Precision optimizer mock), robust plotting (PDF only),
# and a fast test harness that runs on CPU in seconds.
#
# Heavy variants with HuggingFace models/datasets are provided as optional
# functions (guarded by try/except) so the script remains runnable without
# internet access. The quick test runs on synthetic data.
#
# REQUIRED LIBRARIES (install before running full experiments):
# - torch (PyTorch)
# - numpy
# - matplotlib
# - seaborn
# - scikit-learn
# - tqdm
# - psutil
# Optional for full HF experiments:
# - transformers
# - datasets
# - peft
# - bitsandbytes
# - evaluate
# - accelerate
# - fairscale (optional)
# - xformers (optional)
#
# All plots are saved as .pdf using bbox_inches="tight".
#
# Usage:
#   - To run the fast test: simply execute this script (it calls quick_test()).
#   - To run full experiments: call run_experiment1(), run_experiment2(), run_experiment3().
#     You may need to customize model names and ensure HF libs are installed.

import os
import math
import json
import time
import random
import shutil
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

try:
    from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix
except Exception:
    confusion_matrix = None

try:
    import psutil
except Exception:
    psutil = None

try:
    # Optional heavy deps
    from transformers import (
        AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForSequenceClassification,
        Trainer, TrainingArguments, DataCollatorWithPadding, DataCollatorForLanguageModeling
    )
    from datasets import load_dataset
    HF_AVAILABLE = True
except Exception:
    HF_AVAILABLE = False

# ---------------------
# Utility
# ---------------------

def set_seed(seed: int = 0):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False


def device_info():
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        return torch.device("cuda"), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)
    return torch.device("cpu"), "cpu"


def peak_mem_gb():
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        peak = max(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved())
        return peak / (1024**3)
    # Fallback: process RSS (host memory) if CUDA not available
    if psutil is not None:
        process = psutil.Process(os.getpid())
        return process.memory_info().rss / (1024**3)
    return 0.0


def reset_peak_mem():
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()


# ---------------------
# Synthetic datasets
# ---------------------

class SyntheticSeqClassDataset(Dataset):
    """Sequence classification dataset with multiple patterns.
    Patterns:
      - 'sum_mod_k': label = sum(tokens) % n_classes
      - 'threshold': label = 1 if any(token >= vocab_size//2) else 0 (binary)
      - 'pattern_mix': mixture of rules for robustness
    """
    def __init__(self, n: int, seq_len: int, vocab_size: int, n_classes: int = 3, pattern: str = 'sum_mod_k', seed: int = 0):
        super().__init__()
        set_seed(seed)
        self.n = n
        self.seq_len = seq_len
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.n_classes = n_classes
        self.pattern = pattern
        self.x = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (n, seq_len), dtype=torch.long)
        self.y = self._make_labels(self.x)

    def _make_labels(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.pattern == 'sum_mod_k':
            return (x.sum(dim=1) % self.n_classes).long()
        elif self.pattern == 'threshold':
            y = (x.ge(self.vocab_size // 2).any(dim=1)).long()
            # ensure binary classes
            return y.clamp(0, 1)
        elif self.pattern == 'pattern_mix':
            # Mixed rule per sample for robustness
            half = x.size(0) // 2
            y1 = (x[:half].sum(dim=1) % self.n_classes).long()
            y2 = (x[half:].ge(self.vocab_size // 2).any(dim=1)).long()
            y2 = y2.clamp(0, min(self.n_classes - 1, 1))
            return torch.cat([y1, y2], dim=0)
        else:
            return (x.sum(dim=1) % self.n_classes).long()

    def __len__(self):
        return self.n

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        return {"input_ids": self.x[idx], "labels": self.y[idx]}


class SyntheticLMDataset(Dataset):
    """Simple language modeling dataset: sequences of integers; predict next token.
    """
    def __init__(self, n: int, seq_len: int, vocab_size: int, seed: int = 0):
        super().__init__()
        set_seed(seed)
        self.n = n
        self.seq_len = seq_len
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.x = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (n, seq_len), dtype=torch.long)

    def __len__(self):
        return self.n

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        inp = self.x[idx]
        labels = inp.clone()
        return {"input_ids": inp, "labels": labels}


# ---------------------
# Toy Transformer model
# ---------------------

class ToyBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, d_ff: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(d_model, n_heads, dropout=dropout, batch_first=True)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model),
        )
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, attn_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.ln1(x)
        attn_out, _ = self.attn(h, h, h, need_weights=False, attn_mask=attn_mask)
        x = x + self.dropout(attn_out)
        h = self.ln2(x)
        x = x + self.dropout(self.ff(h))
        return x


class ToyTransformer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 128, n_layers: int = 4, n_heads: int = 4, d_ff: int = 256, max_len: int = 256, task: str = 'cls', n_classes: int = 3):
        super().__init__()
        self.task = task  # 'cls' or 'lm'
        self.n_layers = n_layers
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([ToyBlock(d_model, n_heads, d_ff) for _ in range(n_layers)])
        self.ln_f = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        if task == 'cls':
            self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, n_classes)
        else:
            self.lm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None):
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        pos = torch.arange(0, T, device=input_ids.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(B, T)
        x = self.embed(input_ids) + self.pos_embed(pos)
        for blk in self.blocks:
            x = blk(x)
        x = self.ln_f(x)
        out = {}
        if self.task == 'cls':
            # mean pool
            pooled = x.mean(dim=1)
            logits = self.head(pooled)
            out['logits'] = logits
            if labels is not None:
                loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
                out['loss'] = loss
        else:
            logits = self.lm_head(x)
            out['logits'] = logits
            if labels is not None:
                loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.view(-1, logits.size(-1)), labels.view(-1))
                out['loss'] = loss
        return out


# ---------------------
# LoRA for Toy Transformer
# ---------------------

class LoRALinear(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, linear: nn.Linear, r: int = 8, alpha: float = 16.0, dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.in_features = linear.in_features
        self.out_features = linear.out_features
        self.r = r
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        # Freeze base
        self.weight = linear.weight
        self.bias = linear.bias
        for p in [self.weight, self.bias]:
            if p is not None:
                p.requires_grad = False
        # LoRA params
        self.A = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(self.out_features, r))
        self.B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(r, self.in_features))
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.B, a=math.sqrt(5))
        nn.init.zeros_(self.A)
        self.scaling = alpha / r

    def forward(self, x):
        base = F.linear(x, self.weight, self.bias)
        lora = self.dropout(x) @ self.B.t() @ self.A.t() * self.scaling
        return base + lora


def apply_lora_to_toy(model: ToyTransformer, r: int = 8, alpha: float = 16.0, dropout: float = 0.05):
    # Replace Linear layers in attention (in_proj/out_proj within MultiheadAttention are not directly accessible),
    # so we wrap feedforward linears and final head for demonstration.
    for blk in model.blocks:
        # Wrap the two FF layers inside blk.ff (Sequential: Linear, GELU, Dropout, Linear)
        lin1 = blk.ff[0]
        lin2 = blk.ff[3]
        blk.ff[0] = LoRALinear(lin1, r=r, alpha=alpha, dropout=dropout)
        blk.ff[3] = LoRALinear(lin2, r=r, alpha=alpha, dropout=dropout)
    if model.task == 'cls':
        model.head = LoRALinear(model.head, r=r, alpha=alpha, dropout=dropout)
    else:
        model.lm_head = LoRALinear(model.lm_head, r=r, alpha=alpha, dropout=dropout)
    return model


# ---------------------
# UCT minimal implementation for Toy model
# ---------------------

@dataclass
class LayerPolicy:
    layer_id: int
    variant: str  # 'reversible' | 'projection' | 'store'
    bits: int = 3


class FewBitGrad:
    """Few-Bit Backward via gradient hooks: quantize grads to k-bit symmetric levels."""
    def __init__(self, bits: int = 3):
        assert 2 <= bits <= 8, "bits must be 2..8 for this demo"
        self.bits = bits
        self._handles = []

    def attach(self, model: nn.Module):
        levels = 2 ** self.bits - 1
        scale_eps = 1e-8
        def hook_fn(grad):
            if grad is None:
                return None
            with torch.no_grad():
                gmax = grad.abs().amax()
                s = gmax / (levels / 2) + scale_eps
                q = torch.clamp((grad / s).round(), min=-(levels//2), max=(levels//2))
                deq = q * s
                return deq
        for p in model.parameters():
            if p.requires_grad:
                self._handles.append(p.register_hook(hook_fn))

    def detach(self):
        for h in self._handles:
            h.remove()
        self._handles.clear()


class AnyPrecisionAdamW(torch.optim.Optimizer):
    """Simplified Any-Precision AdamW with quantized moments.
    Stores m and v as int8 with dynamic scale; supports logical bits in {2,4,8}.
    Up-scales if loss diverges (provided via update_loss()).
    """
    def __init__(self, params, lr=1e-3, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.01, ap_bits: int = 8):
        defaults = dict(lr=lr, betas=betas, eps=eps, weight_decay=weight_decay)
        super().__init__(params, defaults)
        assert ap_bits in (2,4,8)
        self.ap_bits = ap_bits
        self._levels = 2 ** ap_bits - 1
        self._loss_window: List[float] = []
        self._divergence_hits = 0

    def state_init(self, p):
        st = self.state[p]
        if 'step' not in st:
            st['step'] = 0
            st['m_q'] = torch.zeros_like(p.data, dtype=torch.int8, device=p.device)
            st['v_q'] = torch.zeros_like(p.data, dtype=torch.int8, device=p.device)
            st['m_s'] = torch.ones(1, device=p.device) * 1e-3
            st['v_s'] = torch.ones(1, device=p.device) * 1e-3

    def _quantize(self, t: torch.Tensor, levels: int):
        gmax = t.abs().amax()
        s = gmax / (levels / 2 + 1e-8) + 1e-8
        q = torch.clamp((t / s).round(), min=-(levels//2), max=(levels//2)).to(torch.int8)
        return q, s

    def _dequantize(self, q: torch.Tensor, s: torch.Tensor):
        return q.float() * s

    def step(self, closure=None):
        loss = None
        if closure is not None:
            with torch.enable_grad():
                loss = closure()
        levels = self._levels
        for group in self.param_groups:
            lr = group['lr']
            beta1, beta2 = group['betas']
            eps = group['eps']
            wd = group['weight_decay']
            for p in group['params']:
                if p.grad is None:
                    continue
                self.state_init(p)
                st = self.state[p]
                st['step'] += 1
                grad = p.grad.data
                if wd != 0:
                    grad = grad.add(p.data, alpha=wd)
                # moments (in float)
                m = self._dequantize(st['m_q'], st['m_s'])
                v = self._dequantize(st['v_q'], st['v_s'])
                m = beta1 * m + (1 - beta1) * grad
                v = beta2 * v + (1 - beta2) * (grad * grad)
                # re-quantize
                st['m_q'], st['m_s'] = self._quantize(m, levels)
                st['v_q'], st['v_s'] = self._quantize(v, levels)
                # bias correction (approx)
                m_hat = m / (1 - beta1 ** st['step'])
                v_hat = v / (1 - beta2 ** st['step'])
                p.data.addcdiv_(m_hat, (v_hat.sqrt() + eps), value=-lr)
        return loss

    def update_loss(self, current_loss: float):
        # Track recent losses and escalate if divergent
        self._loss_window.append(float(current_loss))
        if len(self._loss_window) > 10:
            self._loss_window.pop(0)
        if len(self._loss_window) >= 5:
            # crude divergence: if running mean increases 3x in a row, upscale
            diffs = [self._loss_window[i+1] - self._loss_window[i] for i in range(len(self._loss_window)-1)]
            if all(d > 0 for d in diffs[-3:]):
                if self.ap_bits < 8:
                    self.ap_bits = 8
                    self._levels = 255
                    self._divergence_hits += 1
                    print(f"[AnyPrecisionAdamW] Upscaled optimizer state precision to 8 bits due to divergence.")


class UCTBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, base_block: ToyBlock, variant: str = 'store'):
        super().__init__()
        self.base = base_block
        assert variant in ('store', 'reversible', 'projection')
        self.variant = variant

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.variant == 'store':
            return self.base(x)
        elif self.variant == 'reversible':
            # Use checkpointing to simulate reversible memory savings
            def fwd(inp):
                return self.base(inp)
            return torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(fwd, x)
        else:  # 'projection'
            # Simulate projected activations: compute base forward, then detach/store 1D projection (no-op for runtime)
            y = self.base(x)
            # Create a tiny projected summary to mimic storing small activations
            # (not used in backward, but logged via hooks in wrapper)
            proj = y.mean(dim=(1, 2))  # [B]
            # Attach as attribute for potential monitoring
            self._last_proj = proj.detach()
            return y


class UCTWrapper(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, model: ToyTransformer, budget_bytes: int, rank: int = 1, bits: int = 3, planner: str = 'greedy', opt_quant: bool = True, controller: bool = True, profile: Optional[Dict] = None):
        super().__init__()
        assert isinstance(model, ToyTransformer), "UCTWrapper supports ToyTransformer in this demo"
        self.model = model
        self.rank = rank
        self.bits = bits
        self.budget_bytes = budget_bytes
        self.controller_on = controller
        self.opt_quant = opt_quant
        self.profile = profile or {"batch_size": 4, "seq_len": 128}
        # Replace blocks with UCTBlocks per planned policy
        self.policy: List[LayerPolicy] = []
        self.controller_events: List[Dict] = []
        self._fewbit = FewBitGrad(bits=self.bits)
        self._attach_fewbit()
        self._plan_layers(planner=planner)

    def _attach_fewbit(self):
        self._fewbit.attach(self.model)

    def _detach_fewbit(self):
        self._fewbit.detach()

    def _estimate_layer_activation_bytes(self, variant: str) -> int:
        # Rough estimate: B * T * D * bytes_per_activation_factor per layer
        B = int(self.profile.get("batch_size", 4))
        T = int(self.profile.get("seq_len", 128))
        D = int(self.model.d_model)
        bytes_fp16 = 2
        # store: full activations; projection: very small rank-1 per token; reversible: near-zero (remat)
        if variant == 'store':
            return B * T * D * bytes_fp16
        elif variant == 'projection':
            return B * self.rank * bytes_fp16
        else:  # reversible
            return B * D * bytes_fp16  # small residual, checkpoint overhead

    def _estimate_optimizer_bytes(self) -> int:
        # AdamW moments (m, v): 2x params; quantized to ap_bits if opt_quant else fp32
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        if self.opt_quant:
            # ap_bits per moment; store int8 (simulate) + scale overhead
            # Approx per param per moment: ap_bits/8 bytes; two moments
            per_param_bytes = (self.bits / 8.0) * 2
        else:
            # two float32 tensors
            per_param_bytes = 4.0 * 2
        return int(total_params * per_param_bytes)

    def estimate_peak_memory_bytes(self) -> int:
        # Rough peak = params (fp16) + activations sum across layers (choose max variant) + optimizer
        param_bytes = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters()) * 2  # fp16
        act_bytes = 0
        for pol in self.policy:
            act_bytes += self._estimate_layer_activation_bytes(pol.variant)
        opt_bytes = self._estimate_optimizer_bytes()
        # plus some overhead
        return int(param_bytes + act_bytes + opt_bytes + 5 * 1024**2)

    def _plan_layers(self, planner: Optional[str] = 'greedy'):
        # Greedy planner: bottom layers -> projection, top layers -> reversible, middle -> store until budget fits
        L = self.model.n_layers
        provisional = []
        for i in range(L):
            if planner is None:
                provisional.append(LayerPolicy(i, 'store', self.bits))
            else:
                if i < L // 3:
                    provisional.append(LayerPolicy(i, 'projection', self.bits))
                elif i >= 2 * L // 3:
                    provisional.append(LayerPolicy(i, 'reversible', self.bits))
                else:
                    provisional.append(LayerPolicy(i, 'store', self.bits))
        self.policy = provisional
        # Enforce budget by flipping middle layers to reversible if needed
        planned = self.estimate_peak_memory_bytes()
        while planned > self.budget_bytes:
            # find a non-reversible layer with largest act cost and switch to reversible
            costs = [(i, self._estimate_layer_activation_bytes(pol.variant)) for i, pol in enumerate(self.policy)]
            idx_sorted = sorted(range(len(costs)), key=lambda k: costs[k][1], reverse=True)
            flipped = False
            for k in idx_sorted:
                if self.policy[k].variant != 'reversible':
                    self.policy[k].variant = 'reversible'
                    flipped = True
                    break
            if not flipped:
                break
            planned = self.estimate_peak_memory_bytes()
        # Apply wrapper blocks to model
        new_blocks = nn.ModuleList()
        for i, blk in enumerate(self.model.blocks):
            new_blocks.append(UCTBlock(blk, variant=self.policy[i].variant))
        self.model.blocks = new_blocks

    def get_policy(self) -> List[Dict]:
        return [dict(layer_id=p.layer_id, variant=p.variant, bits=p.bits) for p in self.policy]

    def set_uniform_policy(self, variant: str):
        assert variant in ('store', 'reversible', 'projection')
        for p in self.policy:
            p.variant = variant
        new_blocks = nn.ModuleList([UCTBlock(blk.base if isinstance(blk, UCTBlock) else blk, variant=variant)
                                    for blk in self.model.blocks])
        self.model.blocks = new_blocks

    def maybe_controller_switch(self, last_peak_bytes: int):
        if not self.controller_on:
            return
        if last_peak_bytes <= self.budget_bytes:
            return
        # Switch the worst-cost non-reversible layer to reversible
        costs = [(i, self._estimate_layer_activation_bytes(pol.variant)) for i, pol in enumerate(self.policy)]
        idx_sorted = sorted(range(len(costs)), key=lambda k: costs[k][1], reverse=True)
        for k in idx_sorted:
            if self.policy[k].variant != 'reversible':
                old = self.policy[k].variant
                self.policy[k].variant = 'reversible'
                # swap block
                blk = self.model.blocks[k]
                base_blk = blk.base if isinstance(blk, UCTBlock) else blk
                self.model.blocks[k] = UCTBlock(base_blk, variant='reversible')
                self.controller_events.append({
                    'layer_id': k, 'old': old, 'new': 'reversible',
                    'time': time.time(), 'peak_bytes': last_peak_bytes
                })
                print(f"[UCT Controller] Switched layer {k} from {old} to reversible due to peak {last_peak_bytes/1e6:.2f} MB exceeding budget {self.budget_bytes/1e6:.2f} MB")
                break

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None):
        return self.model(input_ids=input_ids, labels=labels)


# Public UCT API (as described in the problem statement)

def uct_wrap(model: ToyTransformer, budget: int, rank: int = 1, bits: int = 3, planner: Optional[str] = 'greedy', opt_quant: bool = True, controller: bool = True, profile: Optional[Dict] = None) -> UCTWrapper:
    return UCTWrapper(model, budget_bytes=budget, rank=rank, bits=bits, planner=planner, opt_quant=opt_quant, controller=controller, profile=profile)


def uct_get_policy(wrapper: UCTWrapper) -> List[Dict]:
    return wrapper.get_policy()


def uct_estimate_peak_memory(wrapper: UCTWrapper) -> int:
    return wrapper.estimate_peak_memory_bytes()


def uct_set_uniform_policy(wrapper: UCTWrapper, variant: str):
    wrapper.set_uniform_policy(variant)


def uct_get_controller_events(wrapper: UCTWrapper) -> List[Dict]:
    return wrapper.controller_events


# ---------------------
# Training utilities for Toy model
# ---------------------

def train_one_epoch(model: nn.Module, opt: torch.optim.Optimizer, loader: DataLoader, device: torch.device, controller: Optional[UCTWrapper] = None) -> Tuple[float, float, int]:
    model.train()
    total_loss = 0.0
    total_correct = 0
    total_count = 0
    total_tokens = 0
    t0 = time.time()
    reset_peak_mem()
    for batch in loader:
        x = batch['input_ids'].to(device)
        y = batch['labels'].to(device)
        out = model(x, labels=y)
        loss = out['loss']
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
        total_loss += float(loss.item()) * x.size(0)
        total_tokens += int(x.numel())
        if 'logits' in out and out['logits'].dim() == 2:  # classification
            preds = out['logits'].argmax(dim=-1)
            total_correct += int((preds == y).sum().item())
            total_count += int(x.size(0))
        # Controller check
        if controller is not None:
            last_peak = peak_mem_gb() * (1024**3)
            controller.maybe_controller_switch(int(last_peak))
    dt = time.time() - t0
    avg_loss = total_loss / max(1, len(loader.dataset))
    acc = (total_correct / total_count) if total_count > 0 else float('nan')
    tps = total_tokens / max(dt, 1e-9)
    return avg_loss, acc, tps


def evaluate(model: nn.Module, loader: DataLoader, device: torch.device) -> Tuple[float, float, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    model.eval()
    total_loss = 0.0
    total_correct = 0
    total_count = 0
    ys = []
    ps = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch in loader:
            x = batch['input_ids'].to(device)
            y = batch['labels'].to(device)
            out = model(x, labels=y)
            loss = out['loss']
            total_loss += float(loss.item()) * x.size(0)
            if 'logits' in out and out['logits'].dim() == 2:  # classification
                preds = out['logits'].argmax(dim=-1)
                total_correct += int((preds == y).sum().item())
                total_count += int(x.size(0))
                ys.append(y.detach().cpu().numpy())
                ps.append(preds.detach().cpu().numpy())
    avg_loss = total_loss / max(1, len(loader.dataset))
    acc = (total_correct / total_count) if total_count > 0 else float('nan')
    y_true = np.concatenate(ys) if ys else np.array([])
    y_pred = np.concatenate(ps) if ps else np.array([])
    return avg_loss, acc, y_true, y_pred
